items: Distributed, reliable, highly available messaging system.
Messages are appended in order to partition logs.
Supports low latency message delivery (usually milliseconds).
Installed as a cluster of brokers (not recommended on a single server for production).
Kafka topics are split into partitions for scalability and parallelism.
Producer API: Sends messages to Kafka topics.
Consumer API: Reads messages from Kafka topics.
Stream API: Processes streams of data in real-time.
Connect API: Integrates Kafka with external systems (e.g., databases).
Specify brokers via bootstrap.servers config.
Send messages to topics with optional key & partition.
Can specify the partition explicitly in ProducerRecord.
Use a custom partitioner for advanced routing.
Use keys to send related messages to the same partition (default hashing partitioner).
Consumers belong to Consumer Groups identified by a group ID.
Each partition is consumed by only one consumer in the group (load balancing).
Consumers can read messages from any offset (not only sequentially).
Consumers use offsets to track the position in a partition.
Best practice: Number of consumers ≤ number of partitions.
bootstrap.servers — List of Kafka broker addresses.
group.id — Consumer group ID.
key.serializer / value.serializer — For Producer message serialization.
key.deserializer / value.deserializer — For Consumer message deserialization.
